paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when the darkest moment shows up, God is already working in the quiet. Athaliah sets out to annihilate all the royal heirs (2 Kings 11:1), and it looks like the line of David is done. But Jehosheba steals Joash away and hides him, and "he was not killed" (2 Kings 11:2). Nobody in that bedroom could see the whole plan, and they didn't need to.

Now look at how the plan gets carried out. Joash stays hidden in the house of the LORD for six years (2 Kings 11:3), and then in the seventh year Jehoiada brings out the king's son (2 Kings 11:4, 12). Six years of waiting is a LONG time, friend, and I know a little about sitting in the dark and wondering. But hidden does not mean forgotten, and slow does not mean stuck. Ordinary people like a sister, a nurse, a priest and a team of guards each did their one piece, and that one piece mattered.

And once the king is crowned, the people don't just celebrate. Jehoiada makes a covenant "that they would be the LORD's people" (2 Kings 11:17), and then they tear down the temple of Baal (2 Kings 11:18). The lesson for you, baker, is to trust God in the hidden stretches, do the piece in front of you faithfully, and clear out whatever competes with Him. It's the same kind of getting ready I'm after in my bakery, where we keep the ovens warm for the big day. And this young king's story is only getting started.
